What your homepage says instead

Your homepage headline today

“Transform Your Home with Expert Painting Services”

What it could say

“Houston house painters for over 20 years. Rated 5.0 by 58 neighbors.”

  • Google, Yelp and Facebook disagree

    Google puts you in the River Oaks Shopping Center, Yelp in West University, and Facebook lists you as a “Wholesale & Supply Store.” Matching details are one of the signals Google uses to rank local businesses.

  • A web address that doesn’t say your name

    Customers who hear “A1 Painting” won’t guess nicepainter.com, and Google gets no help connecting the two.

  • Two main headlines on every page

    Your logo is marked as a main heading, so every page leads with “A1 Painting” instead of what the page is about.

  • The contact page has no Google description

    The page where people reach you has no summary for Google to show.

  • A thinner homepage than your rivals

    About 335 words. The painters above you on Maps explain services, areas and process in far more depth.

  • Yelp tells a different story

    4.3 stars from 17 Yelp reviews next to your perfect 5.0 on Google. Worth answering the Yelp reviews.

Choosing interior paint colors that work in Houston light 1. Test samples on two walls and check them morning and evening. 2. Bright Texas sun washes colors out; go a shade deeper than you think. 3. Satin or eggshell hides more than flat in busy rooms. 4. Trim and ceilings in a crisp white make any color look intentional. Free same-day estimate from A1 Painting: (713) 906-4663.
